blocks.description:
Page content blocks (JSON array). Each block shape:
  {id: '<uuid>', type: '<block_type>', data: {...}}

Block types + the `data.*` fields the DEFAULT theme reads:
  • hero            : headline, subheadline, cta_primary:{label,url}, cta_secondary:{label,url}, background_image_url, style
  • features_grid   : headline, columns (int, default 3), features:[{icon, title, description}]
  • cta_section     : headline, description, cta_primary:{label,url}
  • faq             : headline, items:[{question, answer}]
  • rich_text       : html (raw HTML string) OR content (Tiptap JSON doc object — NOT a string)
  • stats_bar       : stats:[{value, label}]
  • testimonials    : headline, testimonials:[{quote, name, role, company}]
  • pricing_table   : headline, plans:[{name, price, period, description, features[], featured, cta:{label,url}}]
  • comparison_table: headline, subheadline, eyebrow, headers:[str] (or columns:[str]), rows:[{label?, cells:[str]}], style, footnote
  • image           : src, alt, caption
  • video_embed     : url, video_id, provider, caption
  • code_example    : title, description, code
  • logo_cloud      : headline, logos:[{src, alt}]
  • spacer          : height (px, default 48)
  • component       : top-level component_slug + props (see content_list_components and content_get_component for that component's props_schema)

🚨 ANTI-PATTERNS that the validator catches loudly:
  - `{type:'rich_text', data:{content:'<string>'}}` → 422 (use data.html)
  - `{type:'rich_text', data:{text:'...'}}` → 422 (use data.html or data.content)
  - `{type:'component', data:{slug:'x'}}` → 422 (top-level component_slug, not data.slug)
  - `{type:'<x>', data:{layout:'...'}}` → 422 (top-level layout, not data.layout)

🚨 SILENT-BLANK-SECTION that the auditor warns about (not blocks the mutation):
  - Wrong field names (title vs headline, items vs features, cta_text vs cta_primary)
    → `_audit.block_level[].rule_id == 'render.unused_field_in_default_theme'` with a 'did you mean' hint per key. Read the auditor output on content_get_page / content_export_page.

canonical_url.description: Canonical URL for duplicate-content consolidation. ≤2048 chars.

collection_type.description:
Which collection a dynamic page binds to. REQUIRED when `template` is 'dynamic_list' or 'dynamic_item'; MUST be null/absent for any other template — backend `_validate_collection_pairing` rejects mismatched pairs either way.

FOUR KINDS OF VALUE ARE ACCEPTED, and they are not equally proven. Rendering status of each:
  · 'posts'  — built-in. Lists at /<page-slug>, items at /blog/<post-slug>. Long-standing.
  · 'docs'   — built-in. Lists at /<page-slug>, items at /docs/<full-path>. Long-standing.
  · 'directory_listings' — built-in. RENDERS: the flat list/detail doors exist and were verified live (2026-09-02) rendering real cards whose count reconciled exactly to the category totals. Gives you a FLAT layout — every published listing on /<page-slug>, each item at /<page-slug>/<listing-slug>, with no category or city in the URL. This coexists with, and does not replace, the nested /{directory_base}/{category}/{city}/{listing} pages that directory_create_category already generates. A listing slug is unique per CATEGORY, not per tenant, so where two categories share one the flat detail door returns a deterministic first match and names the category it chose in `category_slug`.
  · an `idap.*` collection, e.g. 'idap.businesses' — the tenant's own IDAP corpus. The items door was opened for it and verified serving real, tenant-scoped rows (2026-09-03); a source that is registered but not servable (e.g. 'idap.streets') answers 422 DATA_SOURCE_NOT_SERVABLE, and an unregistered one 404s. Bind it and the dynamic_list template iterates those rows.
  · a CUSTOM-COLLECTION SLUG (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$) — any collection you made with collection_create. Accepted and handled: the page reads the collection's published records through the same items door, item URLs are /<collection-slug>/<record-slug>. This has always worked and was simply never documented.

🔴 EXISTENCE IS NOT CHECKED HERE, DELIBERATELY. The validator has no database, so a well-formed slug for a collection that does not exist is ACCEPTED at create time and renders the template's empty state at request time — indistinguishable from a real collection with no published records. Confirm the collection exists (collection_list / list_data_sources) rather than trusting the 201.

confirm_token.description: Token from a prior dry_run call. Single-use, 7d TTL.

dry_run.description: Preview the change without mutating and receive a confirm_token. When omitted, the change is applied immediately (legacy behaviour preserved).

is_folder.description: Create a FOLDER instead of a page. A folder is an organizational node in the page tree — it has no live URL of its own and is never rendered, sitemapped or listed in llms.txt. Put pages under it with content_update_page → parent_id, then point a navigation menu at it with content_update_navigation (source: {kind:'folder', folder_id:<this id>}) so the menu tracks the folder's published children automatically. Default false.

json_ld.description: JSON-LD structured data object, emitted verbatim into a <script type="application/ld+json"> tag.

og_description.description: Open Graph description (social share cards). ≤500 chars.

og_image_url.description: Open Graph / Twitter share image URL (absolute).

og_title.description: Open Graph title (social share cards). ≤200 chars.

project.description: Optional project — a website inside the workspace (proj_xxx) — to scope this call to. Sent as the X-Project-Id header. If omitted, the spideriq.json / SPIDERIQ_PROJECT_ID binding (or the workspace default project) is used.

robots.description: Per-page robots meta — the indexing lever. Format `<index|noindex>,<follow|nofollow>` e.g. 'index,follow' or 'noindex,nofollow'. UNSET ⇒ no robots meta emitted ⇒ indexable by default.

slug.description: URL slug (auto-generated from title if omitted). Flat slugs only — `/` is rejected (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$). Nested URLs not supported for general pages; docs use parent_id chains.

template.description: Page template — selects which themes/default/templates/<template>.liquid the renderer uses. Free string (backend default 'default'). Common values bundled with the default theme: 'default' (standard chrome), 'blank' (no header/footer — full canvas, matches `content_apply_layout_preset preset="blank"`), 'landing' (marketing chrome), 'about', 'contact'. Dynamic page templates (require `collection_type`): 'dynamic_list', 'dynamic_item'. 'dynamic_landing' is the THIRD dynamic template and takes NO collection_type — it is lead-scoped, not collection-scoped: it gains the routes /lp/{slug}/{identifier} and /lp/{slug}/{salesperson}/{identifier}, and the identifier is resolved against IDAP by `place_id` unless the URL adds ?resolve_key=<key> (domain, email, pin_name, vat, lei, tax_id, registration_number, account_id, pin_data_set_id, pin_subscription_id). Preview it at /lp/{slug}/demo (or ?preview=sample-lead): the demo fixture's KEY SET is generated from the same IDAP field manifest the live door serves, so a field that is blank in preview is blank in production too — it is no longer the case that a real column can be silently missing from the fixture. 🔴 Merge tags (`{{ first_name }}`, `{{ business_name }}`, …) are populated on THESE /lp/ routes ONLY; on every other template, including directory pages, they resolve to the canonical empty shape. NOTE: form-page URLs at /f/<flow_id> and booking URLs at /b/<flow_id> are NOT controlled by this field — they use 'forms-standalone' and 'booking-standalone' templates respectively, picked server-side by the /f/ route from the flow's `kind`. To customize form/booking page chrome, override templates/forms-standalone.liquid or templates/booking-standalone.liquid via template_upsert (both extend layout/theme.liquid, so layout overrides apply). Any other string maps to a custom template the client has uploaded via template_upsert.

twitter_card.description: Twitter card type. One of: summary, summary_large_image.

twitter_image_url.description: Twitter-specific share image URL (absolute). Falls back to og_image_url.

workspace.description: Tenant to target (cli_…). Omit to use the active/bound workspace. list_workspaces shows the options.
